MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  NOVEMBER 15, 2016

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 7:10 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Planning Technician/Code Administrator Jessica Slawson

Others Present:  Robert Schachter, Planning Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY  COUNCIL  MINUTES  OF
  OCTOBER 24, 2016 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 25, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 25, 2016 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL requested the following corrections on Page 1:

  “COUNCIL MEMBERS PRESENT: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

  COUNCIL MEMBERS ABSENT:  Mitchell, Zuckerman”

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2016
  AS AMENDED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER AND NOVEMBER

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57586 THROUGH 57647 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,657,714.38; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100116 THROUGH
  100216; 57442 THROUGH 57448; 57480 THROUGH 57505; 57554
  THROUGH 57564 IN THE AMOUNT OF $231,814.74 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,889,529.12 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Brief discussion ensued regarding the cost of County street repairs.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-D.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

B.  SEPTEMBER 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted the City is still waiting for reimbursement from the State and
  County for the Equestrian Center project.

C.  SEPTEMBER MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  FIRST QUARTER BUDGET REVIEW FY 2016-17

  DIRECTED STAFF TO MONITOR THE CITY’S POSITION.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  WEST BASIN DESALINATION PRESENTATION BY  HAROLD  WILLIAMS,
  DIRECTOR AND RICH NAGEL, GENERAL MANAGER

  Harold Williams, Vice President, West Basin Division 1, introduced Shivaji
  Deshmukh, Assistant City Manager, to provide the desalination presentation.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
   Mr. Deshmukh provided an extensive overview of the Ocean Water Desalination
  Project. He noted that, although this plan is not approved for construction,
  they are looking for support from local cities. He further noted that they have
  been working with the public to determine their concerns.

  Extensive discussion ensued regarding, cost, environmental impacts,
  aesthetics, timing, alternative technologies and alternate sources of water.

  Eileen Hupp, President/CEO, Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce, commented
  that they strongly support this project in order to increase local control of the
  water supply, reduce dependency on imported water, and create jobs. She then
  announced that a “Good Morning Palos Verdes” Breakfast is scheduled for
  December 7. Finally she thanked the COUNCIL for considering West Basin’s
  plan and encouraged their support.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted his opinion that it is unusual to ask for support at
  this time since the EIR has not been prepared.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO PROVIDE CONDITIONAL SUPPORT FOR THE WEST BASIN
  DESALINATION PROJECT PENDING ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Zuckerman

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 7, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 7, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  PA-32-16 - CODE ENFORCEMENT PROCEDURES AND PROPOSED
  AMENDMENT TO CHAPTER 1.25 (ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS) OF THE
  RHEMC - ORDINANCE NO. 711

  Recommendation: That the City Council introduce Ordinance No. 711 for first
  reading, and continue it to the next meeting of December 13, 2016 for second
  reading and adoption.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, City Attorney Davis noted that a
  lien and assessment could be placed on a property if compliance is not
  achieved. Planning Director Wahba noted that the City’s primary goal is always
  to achieve compliance.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, City Attorney Davis noted that
  the COUNCIL has some flexibility in placing or removing a lien as warranted.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 711 FOR FIRST READING, AND
  CONTINUE IT TO THE NEXT MEETING OF DECEMBER 13, 2016 FOR
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 711 by title only.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  APPROVAL OF TERMINATION OF CONSTRUCTION, OPERATION AND
  RECIPROCAL EASEMENT AGREEMENT (CONTINENTAL RHE CORP AND
  PALOS VERDES LIBRARY DISTRICT)

  Recommendation:  That the City Council authorize the execution of the
  proposed Termination of Construction, Operation and Reciprocal Easement
  Agreement.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN City Attorney Davis stated that
  the affected parties have already consented and approved this agreement, and
  once it is executed by the City, it would be forwarded to escrow.

  Lisa Kranitz, Continental Development, noted that the Palos Verdes Library
  District and Continental Development have already executed the necessary
  agreements and that all documents will be recorded concurrently.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE THE EXECUTION OF THE PROPOSED TERMINATION
  OF CONSTRUCTION, OPERATION AND RECIPROCAL EASEMENT
  AGREEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  COMMUNITY CHOICE AGGREGATION (CCA) PROGRAM UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report, and once
  the County and South Bay Clean Power Working Group have taken additional
  steps in solidifying timelines for cities to take action, staff will bring back to the
  Council a more detailed discussion of options available to the City.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Senior Planner Naughton noted that
  the South Bay Clean Power Group would provide consultants at no cost. She
  noted that down the line there may be some cost for staffing.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that she would like to receive more
  information before COUNCIL makes a decision on the appropriate approach for
  the City.

  Brief discussion took place regarding the make-up of either the County or the
  South Bay Joint Powers Authority Board.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the County provided a presentation at
  one of their Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting.

  Senior Planner Naughton noted that, if all the cities in the County were to join,
  it would be the largest utility provider in the country.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN ORDERED THIS
  REPORT RECEIVED AND FILED AND DIRECTED STAFF TO BRING BACK A
  MORE DETAILED DISCUSSION OF OPTIONS WHEN AVAILABLE.
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
 C.  VOTER PARTICIPATION: SB 415

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to prepare an ordinance
  establishing a transition plan to comply with SB 415.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted that it seems Option 2 would save the City the
  cost of an extra election. City Manager Prichard noted that the cost per
  consolidated election is approximately $50,000.

  City Attorney Davis noted that he will undertake research to determine if the
  COUNCIL has the ability to extend Council terms.

  After further discussion, MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN stated that it seems
  Option 2 would allow those who run for office to serve four years at a minimum
  and supported this option.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ stated her concern for the cost of an additional
  election with such low voter turnout.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that if the City’s election was combined
  with the state-wide general election in November, local candidates may not be
  able to garner sufficient attention for voters to make an informed decision and
  that she would be in favor of extending existing terms by six months to coincide
  with the state-wide primary elections in June.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the City is a general law city and
  believed that having the elections in June is the easiest way to deal with this
  situation.

  In response to concern expressed by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, City Manager
  Prichard noted that regardless of election date, the City’s budget process would
  continue as before.

  After continued discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL that June
  would be the preferred option with an extension of six months provided that the
  law allows this action.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO:  1) DETERMINE IF THE COUNCIL HAS
  AUTHORITY TO EXTEND COUNCIL MEMBER TERMS AND, 2) IF SO,
  PREPARE AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A TRANSITION PLAN
  CHANGING THE DATE OF ELECTIONS TO JUNE OF EVEN-NUMBERED
  YEARS AND EXTENDING EXISTING COUNCIL TERMS BY SIX MONTHS
  TO COMPLY WITH SB 415.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  City Attorney Davis updated the COUNCIL on a code enforcement case that was
  appealed to the Superior Court and will be heard in December.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her interest in having a discussion regarding
  committee assignments and her wish to be reassigned to the Equestrian
  Committee for continuity.
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL commented that, while it is good to have continuity,
  it is important for all the COUNCIL MEMBERS to experience chairing the various
  committees.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL limit each committee to six at-large
  members.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 24, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  GENERAL PLAN UPDATE – REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP)

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to solicit bids starting
  November 16, 2016, and due by January 20, 2017, for an Update to the City of
  Rolling Hills Estates' General Plan and associated Environmental Impact Report
  (EIR).

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba noted that the
  General Plan lays out the goals and implementation measures which would
  then be incorporated into the Zoning Code.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SOLICIT BIDS STARTING NOVEMBER 16,
  2016, AND DUE BY JANUARY 20, 2017, FOR AN UPDATE TO THE CITY
  OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES' GENERAL PLAN AND ASSOCIATED
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (EIR).

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF announced that the Peninsula Holiday Parade is
  scheduled for Saturday, December 3 from 6:00-8:00 p.m. She noted that the
  streets will be closed beginning at 4:15 p.m.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ announced the Tree Lighting Ceremony and drawing
  for a ride with Santa in the Parade will be held Saturday, November 19 from 4:00-
  5:00 p.m. at The Promenade.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 1, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Make a determination on a case-
  by-case basis as to the reappointment of current Commissioners and
  Committee Members whose terms expire December 31, 2016; 2) Direct staff to
  schedule interviews and/or conduct recruitment as necessary based on actions
  taken under Recommendation 1; 3) Direct staff to recruit for two vacancies on
  the Environmental Advisory Committee; 4) Reconsider the number of at-large
  members of the Equestrian Committee; and 5) Extend the terms of Planning
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 15, 2016
   Commissioners Thomas and Zigrang to expire December 31, 2018 to restore the
  balance to the rolling expiration schedule.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  After extensive discussion, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by
  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE: 1) EXTENDING THE TERMS OF PLANNING
  COMMISSIONERS THOMAS AND ZIGRANG TO DECEMBER, 2018; 2)
  MEETING WITH PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONERS VAN INGEN
  POPE AND ROMANELLI; 3) RECRUITING FOR THE VACANCY ON THE
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION AND ALL COMMITTEES; 4)
  LIMITING AT-LARGE COMMITTEE MEMBERS TO SIX; 5) DELETING THE
  CONCEPT OF “UNEXCUSED” AND “EXCUSED” ABSENCES AND
  COUNTING ONLY ABSENCES; AND 6) CONFIRMING THAT THOSE
  COMMISSIONERS WHO HAVE THREE CONSECUTIVE ABSENCES BE
  AUTOMATICALLY REMOVED FROM COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  60TH ANNIVERSARY SUBCOMMITTEE

  Recommendation: That the City Council establish and appoint representatives
  to the 60th Anniversary Subcommittee.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  City Manager Prichard suggested appointing two COUNCIL MEMBERS, two or
  three Park and Activities Commissioners and have them discuss and decide
  who else to invite to serve on this subcommittee.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL
